chunks: 3 - Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, who said:

Al-Ma'mun said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of God, I have recognized your virtue, your knowledge, your asceticism, your piety, and your worship, and I see that you are more rightful to the caliphate than me. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Through servitude to God, Mighty and Majestic, I take pride; and through asceticism in this world I hope for salvation from the evil of this world; and through piety from the forbidden I hope to win the spoils; and through humility in this world I hope for elevation in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic.

So al-Ma'mun said to him: I have decided to abdicate myself from the caliphate, give it to you, and pledge allegiance to you. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him: If the caliphate were yours and God made it for you, then it is not permissible for you to remove a garment that God dressed you with and give it to someone else. And if the caliphate were not yours, then it is not permissible for you to give me what is not yours. So al-Ma'mun said: O son of the Messenger of God, you must accept this affair. So he said: I will never do that willingly. He did not cease striving for days until he despaired. So he said: If you will not accept the caliphate and do not like my pledge to you, then be my crown prince so that the caliphate will be yours after me.

So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: By God, my father narrated to me from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful, from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family): I will leave this world before you, killed by poison, oppressed. The angels of the heavens and the earth will weep for me, and I will be buried in a land of exile beside Harun al-Rashid. Al-Ma'mun wept, then asked who would kill him. Al-Rida said he could name his killer if he wished. Al-Ma'mun accused him of using these words to avoid the affair. Al-Rida swore he had never lied, and revealed al-Ma'mun's true motive: to make people say that Ali ibn Musa accepted the crown prince position out of worldly desire, not asceticism.

So al-Ma'mun became angry, then said: You always treat me in a way that I hate, and you have felt safe from my authority. I swear by God, you must accept the position of crown prince, or I will force you; and if you do not, I will strike your neck. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: God, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited me from casting my hand into peril. If the matter is as such, then do as you wish, and I accept that, on condition that I do not appoint anyone, nor dismiss anyone, nor change any practice or tradition, and that I remain as a distant advisor.

So he accepted that from him, and made him his crown prince despite his (peace be upon him) dislike of that (1). And may God bless His Messenger Muhammad and his pure and purified family, and grant abundant peace.

key_terms.التهلكة: Peril / destruction - reference to Quran 2:195 prohibiting self-destruction
key_terms.الخلافة: The caliphate - supreme political-religious leadership of the Muslim community

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Rida accept the position of crown prince under al-Ma'mun?
ai.summary: This famous narration records the dialogue between the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun and Imam al-Rida (AS) regarding the caliphate and the position of crown prince. Al-Ma'mun first offers the caliphate itself, which al-Rida rejects with a devastating logical argument. When al-Ma'mun then proposes the crown prince position, al-Rida prophesies his own martyrdom by poison. Finally, under threat of death, al-Rida accepts the title only nominally, stipulating conditions that effectively strip it of real authority. The narration reveals the political pressures the Imams faced and al-Rida's profound awareness of his own fate.
